title: A tower of non-retractable first order deformations
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal F$ be fibred in groupoids on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. A category fibred in groupoids assigns a groupoid $\mathcal F(T)$ to each scheme $T$ over the base, with pullback functors and coherent identity and composition isomorphisms. Assume also that for every diagram of base algebras $A\to B\leftarrow B'$ with $B'\to B$ surjective and square-zero kernel, restriction gives an equivalence $\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_B B'))\simeq\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)\times_{\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B)}\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B')$, where the right side retains the specified isomorphism over $B$ and arrows compatible with it. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ be affine of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, let $x\in\mathcal F(U)$, and let $(u_n)_{n\geq1}$ be finite type points of $U$ such that no two distinct terms specialize to one another and $x$ is not versal at any $u_n$. A point $u\in U$ is of finite type if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-residue-field]. For $x\in\mathcal F(U)$, versality at $u$ means: for every surjection $A'\to A$ of Artinian local base algebras with common residue field identified with $\kappa(u)$ and nilpotent kernel, every map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$, and every $y'\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A')$ with a specified isomorphism $y'|_A\cong x|_A$, there is a lift $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism $y'\cong x|_{A'}$ inducing the specified one. Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize; local means having a unique maximal ideal, and all maps respect the residue-field identifications. Then there exist a sequence of surjective ring maps $R_n\to R_{n-1}$ and a compatible system $x_n\in\mathcal F(U_n)$, where $U_n=\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ and $x_0=x$, with specified isomorphisms $x_n|_{U_{n-1}}\cong x_{n-1}$. Each composite $R_n\to R_0$ has square-zero kernel, so all $U_n$ have the same underlying space as $U$. For every $n\geq1$ there is no open neighbourhood $W\subseteq U_n$ of $u_n$, no morphism $r:W\to U$ whose restriction to $U\cap W$ is its open inclusion in $U$, and no isomorphism $\alpha:x_n|_W\cong r^*x$ whose restriction to $U\cap W$ is the inverse of the specified reduction isomorphism $r^*x|_{U\cap W}\cong x_n|_{U\cap W}$. Equivalently, there is no cartesian arrow $x_n|_W\to x$ whose composition with $x|_{U\cap W}\to x_n|_W$ is the canonical restriction arrow. The maps $U\to U_n$ are first order thickenings [def-sbc-first-order-thickening].

source.place: Tag 0G2S (lemma-infinite-sequence-pre), specialized to Spec Z; conditions (1) and (3), with the affine spectra used in the proof of Tag 0CXU. The residue-field kernel clause (2) is not needed here.

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$ apply [lem-sfb-artin-single-point-obstruction] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, the given $U,x$, and $u=u_n$. The integers are Noetherian since every ideal is principal, and the remaining hypotheses are precisely the finite-type, nonversality and square-zero gluing hypotheses of the item. Choose a surjection $q_n:S_n\to R_0$ with square-zero kernel $I_n\cong\kappa(u_n)$, an object $y_n\in\mathcal F(T_n)$ for $T_n=\operatorname{Spec}S_n$, and its specified reduction isomorphism to $x$. The cited statement forbids, on every neighbourhood of $u_n$ in $T_n$, an arrow $y_n\to x$ whose composite with $x\to y_n$ is the canonical restriction arrow.

source.place: Tag 0G2S (lemma-infinite-sequence-pre), proof, using Tag 0G2J (lemma-single-point); explicit affine fibre-product construction.

proof.text: Set $R_0$ as given and, for $n\geq1$, define the commutative ring $R_n=\{(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\in\prod_{i=1}^n S_i:q_1(s_1)=\cdots=q_n(s_n)\}$ with coordinatewise operations; its map to $R_0$ is the common value. Forgetting the last coordinate gives $R_n\to R_{n-1}$ (for $n=1$ use $q_1$). This map is surjective: lift the common value to $S_n$. The map to $R_0$ is likewise surjective by choosing finitely many lifts. Its kernel is $\prod_{i=1}^n I_i$, whose product is zero because multiplication is coordinatewise and $I_i^2=0$. Thus $U=\operatorname{Spec}R_0\to U_n=\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ is a first order thickening by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] and the affine description of closed immersions in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. In particular all these schemes have the same underlying space: every prime contains the square-zero kernel. The coordinate projections induce maps $T_i\to U_n$ for $1\leq i\leq n$, whose composite with $U\to T_i$ is $U\to U_n$, by the functoriality of [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 0G2S (lemma-infinite-sequence-pre), proof, using Tag 0G2J (lemma-single-point); explicit affine fibre-product construction.

proof.text: Take $x_0=x$ and $x_1=y_1$. For the induction step, $R_n=R_{n-1}\times_{R_0}S_n$, and $S_n\to R_0$ is surjective with square-zero kernel. Apply the assumed restriction equivalence to the pair $(x_{n-1},y_n)$ with their specified identification over $U$. Essential surjectivity gives $x_n\in\mathcal F(U_n)$ and restriction isomorphisms to both objects whose reductions agree with that identification. Choose these at each stage. Composing the transition isomorphisms gives compatible reductions to $x$, and the isomorphism $x_n|_{T_n}\cong y_n$ respects the chosen reduction to $x$. This uses only the gluing equivalence explicitly assumed in the item and its groupoid of pairs with a specified isomorphism; there is no appeal to stack descent.

source.place: Tag 0G2S (lemma-infinite-sequence-pre), proof, using Tag 0G2J (lemma-single-point); explicit affine fibre-product construction.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$ and suppose an open neighbourhood $W\subset U_n$ of $u_n$ admitted the forbidden arrow $x_n|_W\to x$. Let $h_n:T_n\to U_n$ be the map induced by the $n$th coordinate projection. Its restriction to $U$ is the identity, so $V=h_n^{-1}(W)$ is an open neighbourhood of $u_n$ in $T_n$ and $U\cap V=U\cap W$ under the common-space identifications. Pull back the arrow along $V\to W$ and compose with $y_n|_V\cong h_n^*x_n|_V$, using step 3. On $U\cap V$ its composite with $x\to y_n$ is the pullback of the assumed canonical composite for $x\to x_n$, hence is the canonical restriction arrow to $x$. This contradicts the prohibition furnished by [lem-sfb-artin-single-point-obstruction]. In the formulation with $r$ and $\alpha$, the pulled-back map is $r\circ h_n|_V$, and the reduction equality for the pulled-back isomorphism is the same equality. This proves the required non-retraction property at every stage. The argument works for the stated antichain of points; the stronger residue-field transition-kernel clause of Tag 0G2S is not part of this item and is not needed.
